one_liner: AI research notebook that answers questions and builds overviews grounded in user-uploaded sources.
auth_notes: Enterprise API only. Requests carry a Google user OAuth access token (docs use gcloud auth login + gcloud auth print-access-token). The calling user must hold an active Gemini Notebook Enterprise license and the Cloud NotebookLM User role (roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmUser). Adding Google Docs/Slides sources needs Drive access (gcloud auth login --enable-gdrive-access). Service-account use is not documented.
access_notes: Consumer NotebookLM has no public API; the API is NotebookLM Enterprise (renamed Gemini Notebook Enterprise) on Google Cloud (Discovery Engine v1alpha). Licenses are bought in the Cloud console by a user with Cloud NotebookLM Admin + Gemini Enterprise Admin roles: free 14-day full-featured trial (5000 licenses), then monthly/yearly subscription of at least 15 licenses; more than 5000 licenses needs Google sales. Setup also requires the org's identity provider configured in Google Cloud (Cloud Identity or Workforce Identity Federation). Per-license price not stated on the fetched page.
api_breadth_notes: About 10 methods: notebooks.create/get/listRecentlyViewed/batchDelete/share; notebooks.sources.batchCreate/uploadFile/get/batchDelete (Docs, Slides, web URL, YouTube, raw text, PDF/DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/audio/image uploads); a separate audio-overview guide is linked but was not fetched.
mcp_notes: No Google-published NotebookLM MCP found. Community servers (e.g. PleasePrompto/notebooklm-mcp, local npx, drives consumer NotebookLM via Chrome automation; now archived/unmaintained) and several PyPI/npm variants built on unofficial access.
blocker: Needs Enterprise licenses, Cloud project and org IdP setup
notes: API is v1alpha and marked Preview (Pre-GA terms, limited support). Endpoint host is regional (us-/eu-/global-discoveryengine.googleapis.com) and paths need the tenant's project number and location, so each customer must supply config. A toolkit would need Google OAuth scopes covering Cloud (and Drive for Docs/Slides sources); scope verification requirements were not checked. Setup page also fetched: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-notebooklm

one_liner: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes conversations.
auth_notes: Official MCP server uses OAuth scoped to each user (vendor integration page). The REST Public API reportedly uses Bearer API keys created in a workspace Developer tab and does not support OAuth (third-party Scalekit write-up; Otter's own API docs could not be read).
access_notes: Otter pricing page lists 'Otter API & Webhooks' only on the Enterprise (custom-priced, contact sales) tier. The hosted MCP server is listed on every tier including Basic (Free), so OAuth-based read access via MCP is self-serve. One help-center snippet (not fetched, 403) said MCP is an Enterprise feature, which conflicts with the pricing page.
api_breadth_notes: Per third-party source: api.otter.ai/v1 with channels/members, conversations (list, get, file ingest), audio download links, workspace details. MCP exposes 3 read-only tools (search, fetch, get_user_info).
mcp_notes: Vendor-hosted remote server at https://mcp.otter.ai/mcp (URL from third-party sources and search snippet of Otter help article), OAuth per user, read-only; listed as an Otter connector in Claude and ChatGPT directories.
blocker: REST API and webhooks are Enterprise-only; MCP is read-only
notes: Fetch failures: https://otter.ai/api/docs/ returned only a page title (likely JS-rendered); https://help.otter.ai/hc/en-us/articles/35287607569687-Otter-MCP-Server returned 403. REST API details rest on a third-party blog (Scalekit). Practical toolkit path today: wrap the official MCP (OAuth, any plan) for search/transcript retrieval; full REST toolkit needs an Enterprise customer workspace. MCP fetch only returns conversations shared with the user.

one_liner: AI notetaker that records, transcribes and summarizes video meetings.
auth_notes: Per-user API keys from User Settings > API Access, sent as X-Api-Key to https://api.fathom.ai/external/v1. OAuth 2.0 is the documented route for public apps other Fathom users install; registration via a self-serve form (~2 min), apps subject to review for promotion/marketplace. OAuth apps cannot use include_transcript/include_summary on list meetings and must call the transcript/summary endpoints.
access_notes: FAQ: 'API access - keys and webhooks - are included on all plans.' Keys only reach meetings the user recorded or that were shared with them/their team. Rate limits are per key/token with no paid increases.
api_breadth_notes: About 11 operations: list meetings, list meeting types, get summary, get transcript, request download, download status, list teams, list team members, list users/permissions, create webhook, delete webhook. Official TypeScript and Python SDKs, OpenAPI spec.
mcp_notes: Official Fathom MCP server at https://api.fathom.ai/mcp (remote URL used by ChatGPT app, Claude connector and other MCP clients); auth method and tool list not stated on overview page.
notes: Read-mostly API (no write endpoints for meetings). Webhook payload does not identify which user's key it belongs to, so use a distinct destination URL per connected user. Webhooks follow Standard Webhooks signing (per third-party guide). Production redirect URIs need separate OAuth apps; HTTPS required. Quickstart also fetched: https://developers.fathom.ai/quickstart

one_liner: AI academic search engine answering questions from peer-reviewed research papers.
auth_notes: REST API documented with an API key (x-api-key) created at consensus.app/api-mcp. The official hosted MCP server accepts OAuth sign-in or the API key as a Bearer token. Whether the REST endpoints themselves accept OAuth user tokens is not confirmed (docs.consensus.app returned 403).
access_notes: API page: API access 'Included on every paid plan, and Deep includes 5x the usage of Pro.' MCP search tool works without an account (3 papers per search) and with a free account (10 papers, 30 calls/month); thread/research-agent tools need an account or API key; paid plans unlock more results and fields.
api_breadth_notes: GET /v1/search (ranked papers with journal, year, citations, DOI, takeaway, full-text chunks) and POST /v1/threads (async research agent with follow-ups). MCP tools: search, create_thread, get_thread, add_to_thread, find_threads.
mcp_notes: Hosted remote server https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp; repo Consensus-NLP/consensus-mcp self-described as 'Official Consensus MCP server' (MIT). OAuth or Bearer API key.
blocker: API keys need a paid plan; free MCP tier heavily limited
notes: Fetch failures: https://docs.consensus.app/ and https://docs.consensus.app/consensus-mcp returned 403; https://consensus.app/pricing/ fetched but showed no prices or API/MCP details. OAuth (requested) is confirmed for the MCP server; building on the MCP is the simplest OAuth path. Do not confuse with goconsensus.com (demo-automation SaaS with its own OAuth V2 API).

one_liner: Document parsing API that turns PDFs and other files into structured LLM-ready data.
auth_notes: API keys created in Reducto Studio (studio.reducto.ai > API Keys), sent as Authorization: Bearer <key>; SDKs read REDUCTO_API_KEY. Base URL https://platform.reducto.ai. The local MCP package offers an OAuth device-code login that just saves an API key locally.
access_notes: Free Studio signup; Standard pay-as-you-go plan includes $150 in free usage, then per-page rates (e.g. Parse $10/1k pages, Extract $20/1k). Growth/Enterprise add higher rate limits, data residency, VPC/on-prem.
api_breadth_notes: Core operations: upload, parse, extract, split, classify, edit, plus async job variants, job get/list and webhooks; Python/JS SDKs and CLI. Exact endpoint count not verified (roughly 20-30 operations).
mcp_notes: Documented by Reducto: hosted remote server https://mcp.reducto.ai/mcp (Bearer API key, public URLs only) and local package mcp-server-reducto via uvx. 9 tools: get_documentation, upload_file, parse_document, extract_data, split_document, classify_document, edit_document, get_job, list_jobs.
notes: Developer-facing API (no end-user OAuth); toolkit would collect a user-supplied API key. File inputs must be uploaded or given as public URLs. Search results mentioned '15,000 free credits' while the fetched pricing page says '$150 in free usage'; treat exact free allowance as subject to change. https://docs.reducto.ai/quickstart.md returned 404 (index.md variant worked).

one_liner: Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer that plans, writes and ships code.
auth_notes: API v3 uses service-user keys (cog_ prefix, RBAC role, 7/30/90-day or no expiry) created by admins in org or enterprise settings, or personal access tokens; sent as Authorization: Bearer. Legacy apk_ keys (v1/v2) deprecated. No OAuth documented, so end users must paste a key.
access_notes: Plans: Free ($0, limited usage), Pro $20/mo, Max $200/mo, Teams ($80/mo minimum), Enterprise (custom, ACU-billed). The pricing page has a 'Devin API' row but which plans include it could not be read; billing docs do not say. Usage consumes plan quota/credits or ACUs.
api_breadth_notes: v3 REST at https://api.devin.ai/v3/organizations/{org_id}/...: sessions (create, message, events), playbooks, knowledge, schedules, integrations, service users and enterprise admin; MCP exposes ~20 tools across these groups plus DeepWiki repo docs.
mcp_notes: Official remote server https://mcp.devin.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP; /sse deprecated). Requires cog_ service-user key or PAT as Bearer; enterprise keys/PATs need X-Org-Id header. Tools: wiki read/ask, devin_session_create/search/interact/events, playbook/knowledge/schedule/automation/review/code-scan manage, user list. Separate free public DeepWiki MCP exists.
blocker: Plan eligibility for API keys unclear; usage consumes paid quota
notes: Also fetched https://docs.devin.ai/admin/billing/self-serve.md and the Cognition plan announcement (https://cognition.com/blog/new-self-serve-plans-for-devin); neither states which plans include API access. Pro/Max are single-user orgs. Long-running async sessions: toolkit should create a session then poll events.

one_liner: Generative AI suite for creating images and videos across many models.
auth_notes: Developer API: credential = key ID + secret from console.higgsfield.ai, sent as 'Authorization: Key KEY_ID:KEY_SECRET' (legacy hf-api-key/hf-secret headers still work); server-side only. The CLI (higgsfield auth login) and hosted MCP use Higgsfield account sign-in with no API key; exact flow (likely OAuth for the MCP connector) not confirmed in fetched pages.
access_notes: Console signup is self-serve, but the API is pay-as-you-go from a prepaid balance (pay per generation; failed requests not charged); no free credits mentioned. Invoice billing only for committed-use contracts. CLI/MCP use consumer plan credits, and help center says unlimited/free generations do not apply to them.
api_breadth_notes: Async queue model: submit to per-model image/video endpoints at https://api.higgsfield.ai, then poll request status or receive webhook; MCP advertises 35+ models and tools. Exact endpoint count not verified.
mcp_notes: Vendor-hosted remote server https://mcp.higgsfield.ai/mcp (Higgsfield's own MCP & CLI page), 'no API key required' (account sign-in), works with Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP clients; consumes plan credits.
blocker: API needs prepaid balance; no free credits documented
notes: Two separate products: the developer API (key+secret, prepaid USD balance) and the consumer account used by CLI/MCP (plan credits). CLI page fetched: https://higgsfield.ai/creator-hub/help-center/integrations/how-do-i-access-higgsfield-via-cli. Two help-center MCP setup pages returned 404. The PyPI package 'higgsfield-cli' is unofficial.

one_liner: Command-line tool that renders Mermaid diagram text to SVG, PNG or PDF.
auth_notes: Open-source local tool (MIT); no authentication. The related Mermaid Chart MCP server uses OAuth 2.1 with Dynamic Client Registration or a Mermaid API token.
access_notes: Install via npm (@mermaid-js/mermaid-cli, mmdc), npx, or Docker image (minlag/mermaid-cli, ghcr.io). No hosted API from the mermaid-js project.
api_breadth_notes: One render command (input file or stdin to SVG/PNG/PDF, Markdown code-block conversion, theme/config options) plus a Node run() function not covered by semver.
mcp_notes: mermaid-js/mermaid-cli publishes no MCP. Mermaid Chart (mermaid.ai, commercial home of Mermaid) hosts a remote MCP at https://mcp.mermaid.ai/mcp (SSE at /sse); free Basic account suffices; tools include validate_and_render_mermaid_diagram, get_diagram_title/summary and Mermaid Chart project/diagram CRUD. Many community Mermaid MCPs also exist (e.g. hustcc/mcp-mermaid).
blocker: Local CLI needing headless Chromium; no hosted API
notes: A toolkit must run mmdc in a sandbox with Puppeteer/Chromium (README references puppeteer-config.json), or instead wrap the Mermaid Chart MCP (OAuth, free tier) for render/validate. 'official' MCP rating refers to Mermaid Chart's server, not the CLI repo.

one_liner: Hosted API for YouTube transcripts, search, channel and playlist data.
auth_notes: REST: Authorization: Bearer <sk_ API key> against https://transcriptapi.com/api/v2 (API reference mentions no OAuth). The MCP server additionally supports OAuth 2.1 with Dynamic Client Registration for clients like Claude and ChatGPT. No Google/YouTube Data API key needed.
access_notes: Signup gives 100 free credits, no card. Paid: $5/month for 1,000 credits (200 RPM) or $54/year (300 RPM); top-ups require an active subscription. 1 credit per successful request; some endpoints free.
api_breadth_notes: 13 GET endpoints: youtube/transcript, info, video/metadata, search, channel resolve/info/search/videos/playlists/posts/sections/latest, playlist/videos.
mcp_notes: Remote streamable-HTTP server https://transcriptapi.com/mcp published by the vendor (GitHub ZeroPointRepo/TranscriptAPI-MCP, registry name com.transcriptapi/...), 12 tools; Bearer sk_ key or OAuth 2.1 DCR.
notes: Third-party service (Zero Point Studio), not Google; it fetches YouTube data outside the official YouTube Data API, so there is platform/ToS and reliability risk. Webhooks not mentioned in the full API reference (marked 'no' on that basis). Do not confuse with transcript-yt.com, a different service.

one_liner: AI meeting recorder producing notes, transcripts and shareable clips for customer-facing teams.
auth_notes: OAuth2 authorization code (PKCE supported; required for public clients) with personal or workspace scope; tokens expire and refresh. Personal Access Tokens (non-expiring, personal scope) and Workspace Access Tokens (admin-only, full workspace access). All sent as Authorization: Bearer; every request needs a Public-Api-Version header. Public clients can skip registration by using a Client ID Metadata Document URL as client_id.
access_notes: Support article: personal API access 'Available on every plan, including Free'; Workspace tokens need admin rights on Business/Enterprise. OAuth workspace scope is 'only available to clients verified by Grain'; how to register a confidential OAuth client (self-serve vs approval) is not stated.
api_breadth_notes: 44 documented endpoints in 9 groups: recordings (incl. transcript txt/vtt/srt, download, tags, sharing), clips, stories, playlists, uploads, hooks, users, teams, meeting types, OAuth token. Rate limit 300 req/min per token.
mcp_notes: Grain-hosted remote MCP for Claude.ai and other chat clients (developers.grain.com/mcp); URL https://api.grain.com/_/mcp per search results (not shown on fetched page). Personal-scope tokens (OAuth or PAT) accepted; workspace tokens not accepted. Read-oriented tools (meetings, notes, transcripts, people, companies, deals).
blocker: Workspace OAuth scope needs Grain verification
notes: Personal-scope toolkit is buildable today with PAT or OAuth; workspace-wide access needs Grain verification of the OAuth client. v1 (beta) API sunset Sept 2026; use v2. API version header value differs across pages (support article: 2025-10-31; developer docs example: 2026-10-01). Developer home also fetched: https://developers.grain.com/
